question: How many patients with a normal RF don't have thrombosis?
evidence: normal RF refers to RF < 20; don't have thrombosis refers to Thrombosis = '0';
clarification: Count every row, including repeated ID values.
gold: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RF < 20 AND T1.Thrombosis = 0
gold0: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RF < 20 AND T1.Thrombosis = 0

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient AS P INNER JOIN Examination AS E ON P.ID = E.ID INNER JOIN Laboratory AS L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.RF < 20 AND E.Thrombosis = 0

b.request: Count all joined Laboratory–Examination records (every row, with repeated patient IDs counted each time) where RF < 20 and Thrombosis = 0, rather than counting distinct patients
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory AS L INNER JOIN Examination AS E ON L.ID = E.ID WHERE L.RF < 20 AND E.Thrombosis = 0

d.request: How many patients with a normal RF (RF < 20) don't have thrombosis (Thrombosis = '0'), counting every row, including repeated ID values rather than only distinct IDs?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination E JOIN Laboratory L ON E.ID = L.ID WHERE CAST(L.RF AS REAL) < 20 AND E.Thrombosis = 0
